1. Explicitly at line 177 in shutdown() 
2. Again at line 186 when ~Application() calls shutdown()

This causes a double-free of the heap_memory pointer. The crash manifests only in release mode due to optimization differences in how the double-free is handled.

Your fix strategy should focus on preventing the double-destruction from user.cpp, not on initializing stdlib features early. Since you cannot modify main.cpp, you need to find a way to intervene in the lifecycle from user.cpp to prevent the second destructor call from operating on already-freed memory.

The static libstdc++ object theory is a different hypothesis - the memory bank points to the simpler double-destruction pattern as the root cause.
